title: Call QA and coaching engine

steps.title: Pull yesterday's recordings
steps.what: Loaded 12 transcribed calls (synthetic) from the VoIP export.
steps.output:
REP: Hi, this is Dana Ortiz from Voxly. Thanks for taking the call.
PROSPECT: Sure. I'm the office manager at Harbor Credit Union.
REP: Before I pitch anything, can you walk me through how calls get routed today?
PROSPECT: Okay, that makes sense.

steps.title: Write the rubric as a JSON schema
steps.what: Sales leaders' five criteria become a Pydantic schema, so every score is comparable.
steps.code:
class CallScore(BaseModel):
    call_id: str
    criteria: list[Criterion]
    total: int
    compliance_flag: bool
    coaching_tips: list[str]
steps.output:
{
  "Discovery": "Asks open questions about the current process and its cost",
  "Active listening": "Plays the pain back in the prospect's words",
  "Value over features": "Links the product to the prospect's pain, not a feature list",
  "Next step": "Books a dated next step with the right people",
  "Compliance": "No misleading statements about recording, pricing or guarantees"
}

steps.title: Score every call in one overnight batch
steps.what: 12 calls sent through the Message Batches API (50% cheaper, results by morning).

steps.title: Post scores and three tips to the CRM
steps.what: An n8n webhook (simulated here) writes a note to each call's CRM record.
steps.output:
QA score 40/100
Coaching:
- Repeat the prospect's pain back in their words before pitching.
- Swap the feature list for one sentence tying Voxly to their pain.
- End every call with a dated meeting and named attendees.

QA score 0/100 | COMPLIANCE FLAG
Coaching:
- Open with two process questions before any product talk.
- Repeat the prospect's pain back in their words before pitching.
- Swap the feature list for one sentence tying Voxly to their pain.

steps.title: Check calls by hand against Claude's scores
steps.what: A manager's hand scores are the answer key. Agreement = within 15 points.
steps.code: agree = mean(abs(model - manager) <= 15 for each call)

steps.title: Tune the prompt, then score again
steps.what: Added three manager-scored anchor calls to the prompt as calibration, then re-ran the batch.

story.situation: A 40-rep UCaaS sales floor. Managers hear about 2% of calls, so coaching is random and compliance misses slip through.
story.constraints: Recordings contain customer PII, so data stays in the company's tenant. Scores must be explainable to reps. Budget favours overnight batch over real-time.
story.replay: Reuse: the rubric-as-schema + batch pattern works for any 'review every X' job (tickets, emails, chats). Next time: calibrate with anchor calls from day one, and track tip adoption per rep.

why: Batch is cheaper for work that can wait, and a schema makes every score comparable.
